inputs.need: For lumbar facet radiofrequency ablation we accept ≥50% relief on a single medial branch block as the selection threshold. Some colleagues insist on ≥80% or on dual blocks. Does the threshold actually change RFA outcomes at 6 months, and could our own follow-up registry answer this without a new prospective study?
inputs.setting: Academic interventional chronic pain clinic, Hamilton, Ontario (Hamilton Health Sciences / McMaster).
inputs.constraints: Not known, and must stay unknown until the investigator supplies it: registry size over the relevant period; proportion of records with percentage relief documented; whether ≥80% and dual-block patients exist in sufficient numbers locally.
localFacts: Fluoroscopic lumbar medial branch blocks and RFA are performed routinely.
A physician assistant performs structured telephone follow-ups that record percentage relief after diagnostic block, NRS pain scores, timestamps and the interval from diagnostic block to RFA.
The investigator is PI and data custodian under PHIPA on existing HiREB-approved studies; the registry's REB status for secondary research use is NOT known.
A trainee is available for a months-long project; the investigator's own hands-on time is 8–15 hours.
Full-text access through the McMaster library; HiREB minimal-risk faculty review typically takes 4–8 weeks.
